authority.legal_name: Helsingin seudun liikenne / Helsinki Region Transport (HSL) — the public transport authority for the Helsinki metropolitan region
authority.geography_type: the Helsinki archipelago and Gulf of Finland shoreline — the city's Market Square, the sea-fortress and recreation islands, the growing Laajasalo waterfront districts, and the regional coast east to Porvoo

mandate.summary: HSL plans and procures public transport for the Helsinki metropolitan region — buses, trams, metro, commuter rail and the public ferry to Suomenlinna. Its ferry mandate is affordable, reliable, year-round island connectivity on a single public ticket, and the decarbonization of every mode it runs.
current_priorities: Connecting the new Laajasalo / Kruunuvuorenranta waterfront residential districts to the centre
Year-round, all-weather island connectivity on the HSL ticket

policy_targets.interim_target: HSL commits to emission-free public transport by 2035 and zero-emission own operations by 2030; the City of Helsinki targets carbon-neutrality by 2035; Finland's Climate Act legislates national net-zero by 2035 — among the world's most ambitious.
policy_targets.vision: An emission-free public transport region where every ferry link is zero-emission and runs on the same HSL ticket as the metro and tram
policy_targets.relevance: HSL has already committed to zero-emission ferries; a foiling-electric platform delivers that on the archipelago links today — fast, low-wake and silent through a sensitive, recreation-heavy waterway, and viable year-round through Baltic conditions.

precedent.headline: HSL already runs the Suomenlinna ferry as public transport and has committed to making it emission-free.

existing_program.program: The year-round Market Square (Kauppatori) → Suomenlinna ferry, part of the HSL public-transport network and ticket, serving the UNESCO World Heritage sea fortress and its residents; HSL's published commitment is emission-free public transport by 2035 and zero-emission operations by 2030
existing_program.proof_stat: A public, ticketed ferry already integral to Helsinki's transit network — the link a foiling-electric fleet decarbonizes and accelerates
existing_program.note: Public transport authority network; the mandate is connectivity + decarbonization, not tourism.

interpretation_for_navier: Anchor on the flagship public ferry (Market Square↔Suomenlinna) and the new Laajasalo commuter waterfront (Market Square↔Kruunuvuorenranta), then the recreation-island network (Vallisaari, Lonna, Korkeasaari Zoo, Pihlajasaari), then the regional line-haul east to Porvoo. Domestic-first. Geometry ALREADY SEALED — bind real route_ids. EXCLUDE the cross-border Helsinki↔Tallinn / ↔Sweden corridors from HSL's domestic arc (outside its mandate).

domestic_network.note: Real atlas boarding points (bp-<hash> / bp-<name>) with real coords; real sealed routes (rn-<hash>) already in ROUTES.json — BIND them. Distances from the sealed atlas.

sealed_pairs.rationale: Market Square ↔ Suomenlinna — HSL's flagship year-round public ferry to the UNESCO sea fortress and its residents.
Market Square ↔ Kruunuvuorenranta (Laajasalo) — the growing waterfront residential district; a genuine commuter link.
Market Square ↔ Vallisaari — recreation-island public access.
Market Square ↔ Lonna — recreation-island public access.
Market Square ↔ Korkeasaari (Zoo Island) — family/recreation public link.
Market Square ↔ Pihlajasaari — recreation-island public access.
Market Square ↔ Porvoo — a regional line-haul east to the historic town where foiling range makes a scheduled coastal service viable.

regional_links.note: Real cross-border corridors exist in the atlas (Helsinki↔Tallinn ~204 nm Quanta-LR; Helsinki↔Sweden) but are OUTSIDE HSL's domestic mandate — EXCLUDED from this authority arc. Also a junk 'Viking Line → Stockholm 2.2nm' leg needs cleanup (mis-scaled).

routing_hazards.instruction: Route the charted archipelago fairways; respect winter sea-ice, dense summer recreational-boat traffic, protected Vallisaari/Pihlajasaari nature areas, and the shallow Kruunuvuorenselkä approaches. Provide explicit hand waypoints for the Suomenlinna and Porvoo approaches.

hazards.detail: The archipelago freezes in winter; year-round service needs ice-capable routing and scheduling (the Suomenlinna ferry runs year-round today).
Vallisaari and Pihlajasaari have protected habitats; low-wake, low-noise approaches matter — a foiling-electric strength.
The inner archipelago is crowded with private craft in summer; route the marked fairways defensively.

hazards.hazard: Shallow, rocky archipelago fairways + Porvoo river approach
hazards.detail: Charted fairways only; the 30 nm Porvoo line-haul ends in a shallow river-quay approach requiring hand waypoints.
